title: Host Analyst (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799), DC I
raw_text:
5.     MOS 1722, Host Analyst (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799), DC I

    a. Summary. This NMOS will be granted upon meeting the United States
Cyber Command training and certification standards for the senior
certification level in this work role. The 1722 NMOS requires knowledge of
operating systems, services, security, and various system configurations
encountered. This work role performs individual memory process analysis
using built-in tools and capabilities. The 1722 NMOS possesses advanced
knowledge of Unix/Linux services and their security and configuration. The
Host Analyst also requires advanced knowledge of file systems, permissions,
and operation system configurations. The Host Analyst develops highly
tailored queries and data visualizations in order gain a battlespace
situational awareness of the endpoint portion of the cyberspace warfighting
domain. The 1722 NMOS is responsible for capturing the memory of individual
processes and analyzing it using built-in tools and capabilities.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must be currently assigned the PMOS of 1721 or 1799.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete training and certification standards as determined by
United States Cyber Command.

        (2) MOS 1722 assigned upon approval of the Director, Information
Maneuver Division.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Defensive Cyberspace Weapons Officer, 1720.

            (2) Cyberspace Warfare Operator, 1721.

            (3) Network Analyst, 1723.

            (4) Cyberspace Warfare Chief, 1799.

The Information Maneuver Occupational Field integrates information capability areas and the military occupational specialties (MOS) of cyberspace, space, electromagnetic warfare, civil affairs, and psychological operations into a single OCCFLD. Marines from these disciplines utilize their exquisite talents, knowledge, skills, and abilities to generate, preserve, and apply informational power against a relevant actor in order to increase or protect competitive advantage or combat power potential within all domains of the operating environment. Duty assignments include Marine Corps Forces Cyberspace Command, Marine Corps Forces Space Command, Marine Corps Information Command, Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion, Marine Corps Information Operations Center, MEF information groups, HQMC, MARFORs, joint organizations, and staff sections at all levels of the MAGTF.

5. MOS 1722, Host Analyst (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799), DC I a. Summary. This NMOS will be granted upon meeting the United States Cyber Command training and certification standards for the senior certification level in this work role. The 1722 NMOS requires knowledge of operating systems, services, security, and various system configurations encountered. This work role performs individual memory process analysis using built-in tools and capabilities. The 1722 NMOS possesses advanced knowledge of Unix/Linux services and their security and configuration. The Host Analyst also requires advanced knowledge of file systems, permissions, and operation system configurations. The Host Analyst develops highly tailored queries and data visualizations in order gain a battlespace situational awareness of the endpoint portion of the cyberspace warfighting domain. The 1722 NMOS is responsible for capturing the memory of individual processes and analyzing it using built-in tools and capabilities. b. Prerequisites. Must be currently assigned the PMOS of 1721 or 1799. c. Requirements (1) Complete training and certification standards as determined by United States Cyber Command. (2) MOS 1722 assigned upon approval of the Director, Information Maneuver Division. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC 3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
